# S-Curve Analysis: Late Maturity

The s-curve for this market has visibly flattened. Adoption velocity has
decayed over the last eight quarters and incremental penetration is bounded by
replacement demand, not new-user demand. This is the structural signature of a
late-growth, mature market.

## Why this contradicts the JTBD finding

However, the mature market framing contradicts the JTBD underservice claim in
[[problem-definition]]. A 20/20 underservice score implies an under-performed
job with unmet demand -- a pattern that should only appear in early or
mid-growth phases of the s-curve, not in a late-growth mature market. Unlike
the problem-definition framing, the market-analysis evidence opposes the
underservice interpretation.

## Triangulation notes

- Late growth normally means incumbents have optimized the primary JTBD.
- A mature market with 20/20 underservice is contradictory on its face.
- Resolving the contradiction requires either re-scoping the JTBD or
  re-scoping the market boundary (see [[solution-design]] for the resolution
  thesis).

## Implications for the venture

- If the mature market framing holds, the underservice must be concentrated in
  a niche, not the whole market.
- If the underservice holds population-wide, the s-curve analysis is wrong.
- The contradiction cannot stand -- one of the two claims has to give.

## Summary

The market is late-growth and mature. The s-curve has flattened. This
directly contradicts the underservice framing in [[problem-definition]] and
forces the venture to either re-scope the market or re-scope the JTBD. Either
way, the contradiction itself is a structural signal the cascade must surface.
